How we work

Every project moves through the same three stages, whether it takes six weeks or a year.

  • 01

    Discover

    We spend the first stretch listening — to leadership, to customers, to the parts of the business the brief left out.

  • 02

    Reframe

    We name the real problem, then build the strategy and creative territory that makes the answer obvious.

  • 03

    Deliver

    Identity, packaging, campaign, product — we take the idea all the way to something a customer can hold.

name: Approach — Brazen

Approach

Four steps. No safety net.

01

Get uncomfortable

We start by finding the opinion your brand is too polite to have, and the market truth your category has been ignoring.

Pick a fight

Build the thing

Make noise

name: About — Fieldmark
html:
About Fieldmark

Fieldmark is a multi-disciplinary, independently owned design studio.

Our work spans brand identity and strategy, products and packaging, exhibitions and environments, websites and digital experiences, advertising and communications, data visualization and typefaces, sound and motion. Our 19 partners are all practicing designers, and whether working together or independently, they do so in partnership.

Our structure is unusual. We are one of the few major design studios where the people who own the business are also the people who do the work and remain the primary contact for every client. This reflects our belief that meaningful design requires passion, intelligence, and above all, personal commitment — and it shows in a body of work that spans four decades, many industries, and clients of every size.

Careers at Fieldmark →

name: Heritage — Fieldmark
html:
Heritage, Reconsidered

Meaningful change rarely means discarding everything that came before. Looking closely at an organization's history often reveals the clearest path to its future. The goal is never a timid, incremental update — it's a confident, energetic distillation of what makes a brand singular.

name: Philosophy — Hollis
html:
Our Philosophy

Most brands settle for average because average is easy. They follow the nearest competitor, soften every edge, and end up sounding like everyone else in their category.

We think a brand should be a considered argument for why it deserves to exist. So we build the case in public — in the name, the voice, the room you walk into, the interface you tap — until the argument is impossible to miss.

Craft over consensus

Committees produce compromises. We keep the room small, the opinions sharp, and the work accountable to one clear point of view.

name: Manifesto A — Werkraum
html:
Werkraum(0)

There was no fallback plan. The fallback was making the plan work.

We moved into Werkraum(0), our first real office, a snug space two streets from the art school. It was a pair of second-hand desks, a shared laser printer we were unreasonably proud of, and a hard drive we backed up onto every Friday without fail.

name: Manifesto B — Werkraum
html:
Werkraum(1)

New studio. New office — Werkraum(1). New faces.

After two years weighing the options, it was time to commit or fold it back into freelancing. My co-founder took a steadier job; I took the leap and made the studio official. Our new chapter opened with three walls' worth of extra desks, a proper server rack, and the unreasonable optimism it takes to sign a five-year lease.
